subject: Next steps: serving lane priorities & capacity path for ShopCart
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Abe Levin <abe@shopcart.io>, Elena Park <elena.park@shopcart.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-10T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + ask: serving lane priorities from today's call

Thanks again for the call today — helpful discussion. Quick recap and concrete asks so we can lock next steps: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary goal: realtime product-search suggestions with strict 99th latency target around 60ms (p50 ~15–20ms) for the user-facing suggestion API.
- Expected steady QPS: 450–700 for US peak windows; batch re-ranks from offline jobs ~150 QPS during non-peak.
- Data sensitivity: PII in prompts is low but procurement wants a VPC option for production later.

Open asks we need from your team to qualify path: 
1) Can you confirm 95th/99th latency SLOs you care about (60ms is our baseline understanding)?
2) Confirm expected sustained concurrent QPS during peak and any monthly burst patterns.
3) Procurement cadence and lead time for reserved capacity (if you prefer Dedicated).

Recommendation options (short):
- Pilot: hosted API with prefix caching + synthetic load test to validate p50/p95. Fast to start (days).
- Production: Dedicated capacity if 99th latency needs hold under sustained peak or if you require single-tenant isolation + committed throughput.
- Private/VPC: can be scheduled after pilot if procurement/regulatory requires on day-1 VPC.

Next step proposal: you share the clarified QPS/SLAs (item 1–2) and we'll send a one-page pilot plan + checklist (attachments) and a tentative calendar for a 2-week pilot run.

Thanks — I can jump on a quick follow-up tomorrow if useful.

— Priyom
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priyom@redwood.com
(415) 555-0198
From: Abe Levin <abe@shopcart.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@shopcart.io>, procurement <procurement@shopcart.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-11T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: serving lane priorities from today's call

Thanks Priyom — useful summary. Answers inline: 

1) Latency: 99th we care about 55–75ms depending on UA (mobile tighter). p50 target 12–20ms. p95 can be up to ~40ms.
2) QPS: Our expectations for US east after GA: sustained 550 QPS peak (weekday evenings), with planned marketing spikes that could double for short windows (~2–3 mins). Average daily QPS ~120.
3) Procurement: If we go Dedicated, standard procurement cycle is ~6–8 weeks for budget approval and ~4 weeks for legal/contract redlines.

Also noted — security wants SOC2 report and an option for a VPC peering setup eventually. For the pilot we are OK with hosted if we validate latency under synthetic load.

Elena will coordinate with procurement; copying her.

— Abe
Abe Levin
Head of Search, ShopCart
abe@shopcart.io
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Abe Levin <abe@shopcart.io>, Elena Park <elena.park@shopcart.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: serving lane priorities from today's call

Great — thanks for the numbers, Abe. With 550 sustained and short double spikes, here's a pragmatic path we see: 

Plan A (recommended):
- Pilot on Hosted API with explicit synthetic load test that models 550 sustained QPS + 2x spike window. We will enable prefix/KV caching and a continuous-batching profile tuned for low-latency small responses. Pilot goal: validate p50/p95/p99 targets for user-facing path.
- If pilot shows 99th consistently >75ms under realistic load, we propose moving to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) — timeline aligns with your procurement window.

Plan B (fast-to-prod reserved):
- If you want dedicated from day-1 due to SLAs or isolation, we can start contract and provisional capacity planning now; procurement timeline you shared (6–8 weeks) fits that.

Operational asks from ShopCart for the pilot: 
- A test token we can use for synthetic load and a small, redacted prompt set reflecting production length (Elena/team).
- Confirmation of one-staging region (us-east) and a calendar week for the pilot start.

I'll attach the quick pilot checklist and a capacity estimate PDF for a 550–1,100 QPS profile. If you prefer, Marissa can run a short calibration run with your dev build next week.

Proposed calendar: pilot prep next week (Jun 21–25), pilot run Jun 28–Jul 9.

— Priyom
From: Elena Park <elena.park@shopcart.io>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@shopcart.io>
Date: 2027-06-13T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + ask: serving lane priorities from today's call

Thanks team — sounds good. A few internal notes from security/procurement: 
- Security: SOC2 cert and a brief writeup on how prefix/KV caching handles customer data; also KMS integrations for key management (if Dedicated/Private).
- Procurement: we'll need a commercial one-pager with pilot terms, pricing assumptions for Hosted vs Dedicated (committed throughput tiers), and a sample SLA for Dedicated.

Procurement lead here — our earliest authorization for any reserved commit will be mid-August. For pilot we can sign a short MSA addendum and run on Hosted.

Please include links for SOC2 and the sample SLA in your one-pager.

— Elena
Elena Park
Senior Product Operations, ShopCart
elena.park@shopcart.io
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Recap + ask: serving lane priorities & capacity path for ShopCart

Appreciate the details — looping to operational owners and next steps: 

Attachments: redwood-quickpilot-checklist.xlsx (pilot runbook), ShopCart_capacity_estimate_v1.pdf (estimated footprint and cost delta Hosted vs Dedicated).

Immediate actions: 
- Priyom/Jordan: please prepare the one-page pilot terms with explicit performance acceptance criteria (p50/p95/p99 thresholds and test scripts) and include the SOC2 link + KMS writeup.
- Elena: confirm pilot token + redacted prompt set and preferred pilot week (we proposed Jun 28 start).
- Procurement: once pilot validates latency, we'll provide a formal Dedicated quote and a sample SLA for review.

If everyone is aligned, I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for Jun 24 to review runbook and test harness — propose Thu Jun 24 10:00 PT. Confirmable by reply.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

— Marissa
